facts.value: Reads the configured XFB count and, when at least two buffers exist, repeatedly inspects global XFB status records under interrupt exclusion. WAITDONE, DRAWDONE, or NEXT produces a continue-wait result; that result causes the caller to sleep until a VI retrace, after which the statuses are sampled again. The function returns no data, exposing completion solely by not returning until those pending statuses disappear.
facts.rationale: The helper disables interrupts around three status searches, converts their disjunction to an integer predicate, restores interrupts, and returns it to the outer loop. The loop consumes that predicate by invoking VIWaitForRetrace and resampling, while the exact VI implementation shows the thread sleeping until retraceCount advances.

evidence.why: Shows the XFB count input, interrupt-protected searches for the three pending statuses, predicate return, and repeated consumption of that predicate.
Shows that each wait transfers control to the VI wait queue until retraceCount advances.

facts.value: Realizes a retrace-paced framebuffer-pipeline barrier: callers can ensure that pending rendered frames have progressed out of GPU-waiting, draw-complete, and next-to-display queue roles before proceeding with operations that require the XFB queue to be flushed.
facts.rationale: The function waits specifically on the HSD presentation states WAITDONE, DRAWDONE, and NEXT and advances time only through VI retraces. Those conditions ground the routine as a barrier for draining queued frame-presentation work rather than a generic delay.

evidence.why: Shows that completion depends on the disappearance of the three outstanding XFB presentation states and that progress is paced by VIWaitForRetrace.
Establishes that the pacing operation synchronizes the caller to advancement of the hardware VI retrace counter.

facts.rationale: The matched definition provides the exact void(void) signature, and its retrace-wait loop establishes that the operation can block.

facts.value: Blocks until the multi-XFB presentation pipeline has no buffer waiting for GX completion, completed but not yet queued, or queued for the next display handoff. It yields between checks by sleeping until the next VI retrace; configurations with fewer than two XFBs require no flush and return immediately.
facts.rationale: The matched function bypasses synchronization when fewer than two XFBs are configured. Otherwise its helper checks for WAITDONE, DRAWDONE, or NEXT buffers and the outer loop calls VIWaitForRetrace while any such buffer remains. The resolved VI routine sleeps until the hardware retrace counter advances, showing that this is a blocking, yielding drain of outstanding presentation work rather than a CPU busy-wait.

evidence.why: Shows the XFB-count fast path and the loop that continues while any XFB has WAITDONE, DRAWDONE, or NEXT status, waiting for a retrace after each positive check.
Shows that VIWaitForRetrace sleeps the calling thread until the VI retrace counter changes.

facts.value: Returns immediately when fewer than two XFBs are configured. Otherwise it remains in a wait-and-recheck state while at least one XFB is WAITDONE, DRAWDONE, or NEXT, sleeping through one or more retraces so draw-done and retrace callbacks can advance the presentation state. It exits as soon as an interrupt-protected snapshot finds none of those three statuses; DISPLAY and other statuses do not by themselves keep this flush active.
facts.rationale: The matched branch and while-loop define the fast path, continuation guard, and termination condition. The helper's predicate names exactly the statuses that prolong waiting, while VIWaitForRetrace proves that each loop iteration waits for retrace progression rather than spinning.

evidence.why: Directly defines the fewer-than-two-buffer guard and the WAITDONE, DRAWDONE, and NEXT continuation states checked under disabled interrupts.
Shows that the wait step completes only after the retrace counter advances.

facts.value: Reads the configured XFB count and, on every poll, searches global HSD video state for XFBs in WAITDONE, DRAWDONE, or NEXT status. Each status snapshot is protected by disabling interrupts and restoring the saved interrupt state. No framebuffer pointer or status is written by this routine; once all three searches fail, control returns to the caller.
facts.rationale: The wrapper's only direct input is the global XFB count. The shared predicate disables interrupts, performs the three status searches, restores the prior interrupt level, and returns a Boolean-like integer consumed by the wrapper's while condition. The absence of assignments to XFB records shows that state advancement must come from asynchronous draw-done or retrace handling rather than this waiter.

evidence.why: Directly shows the global status searches, interrupt-protected snapshot, returned polling condition, XFB-count guard, and lack of framebuffer-state mutation.

facts.value: Provides a hard synchronization point for frame presentation before framebuffer ownership is inspected or handed back: its known caller drains pending rendered and queued frames first, then obtains the last drawn XFB and selects the remaining framebuffer pointers.
facts.rationale: The flush predicate waits on statuses representing outstanding GX completion and VI presentation work. The resolved caller invokes this routine before reading HSD_VIData's last-drawn and remaining XFB pointers, grounding the routine in the low-level frame-buffer handoff rather than general-purpose waiting.

evidence.why: Shows that the synchronization condition is specifically the absence of pending WAITDONE, DRAWDONE, and NEXT XFB states.
Shows the caller draining the XFB pipeline before identifying the last-drawn framebuffer and collecting other framebuffer pointers.

facts.value: Parameterless blocking routine with exact signature void HSD_VIWaitXFBFlushNoYield(void); it communicates completion only by returning after the global XFB queue has drained.
facts.rationale: The matched definition supplies the exact void(void) signature. Its body has no output parameters or return value, so the only observable completion signal to its caller is control returning after the polling loop terminates.

evidence.why: Provides the exact signature and shows that completion is represented solely by return from the loop.
Shows a caller invoking the routine without arguments and proceeding to inspect and return framebuffer pointers only after it returns.

facts.value: Synchronously drains the multi-XFB presentation pipeline without yielding: when at least two external framebuffers are configured, it busy-waits until no XFB remains waiting for GX draw completion, completed but not yet queued, or queued for display.
facts.rationale: The function returns immediately for fewer than two XFBs and otherwise repeatedly calls the shared flush predicate with an empty loop body. That predicate remains true while any XFB has WAITDONE, DRAWDONE, or NEXT status, directly establishing both the drain condition and the non-yielding synchronization role.

evidence.why: Shows the multi-XFB guard, the WAITDONE/DRAWDONE/NEXT flush predicate, and the empty busy-wait loop used by the no-yield variant.

facts.value: If fewer than two XFBs are configured, the function returns immediately. Otherwise it remains in a tight polling loop while any XFB is WAITDONE, DRAWDONE, or NEXT and exits only when none has those statuses. Unlike HSD_VIWaitXFBFlush, it performs no VIWaitForRetrace call between polls and therefore does not voluntarily yield while waiting.
facts.rationale: The guard and empty while body directly define the no-op and busy-wait states. The adjacent yielding variant uses the same guard and predicate but calls VIWaitForRetrace inside its loop, making the behavioral distinction explicit rather than inferred solely from the function name.

evidence.why: Shows the complete guard and loop behavior of both flush variants, including that only the ordinary variant waits for retrace between polls.

facts.value: Initialization imports the requested VI configuration and up to three XFB pointers into global HSD video state and issues the first EFB-to-XFB copy. During subsequent presentation, XFB status values carry buffers through copy completion, queued-next, displayed, and free roles; retrace callbacks advance those roles, release the EFB after a deferred copy, and forward the hardware retrace count to optional user callbacks.
facts.rationale: The current HSD_VIInit stores its VI configuration and framebuffer arguments, initializes each buffer record, installs callbacks, and submits the initial display copy. The post-retrace callback consumes the resulting status records to rotate displayed and queued buffers or finish a deferred EFB copy, then passes the retrace count to the registered user callback.

evidence.why: Shows the VI configuration and three framebuffer pointers entering global video state, status initialization, callback registration, and the initial EFB-to-XFB transfer.
Shows retrace-time XFB status rotation, deferred EFB-copy completion, EFB release, and forwarding of the retrace count to the optional post-retrace callback.

facts.value: Realizes Melee's low-level, retrace-synchronized frame presentation and display reconfiguration: completed frames carry the video settings with which they were produced, and the VI render mode, black state, framebuffer selection, and queue ownership are updated together at retrace boundaries.
facts.rationale: The current frame-completion path snapshots the active video state into the completed XFB record. The pre-retrace callback selects the queued framebuffer and applies its saved render mode and black state before flushing VI, while the post-retrace callback rotates queued and displayed ownership. These operations bind display reconfiguration to retrace-synchronized frame presentation.

evidence.why: Shows completed-frame processing saving the current video configuration into an XFB before that buffer advances toward presentation.
Shows the pre-retrace callback selecting the next framebuffer, applying its saved render mode and black state, flushing VI, and tracking frame renewal.
Shows the post-retrace callback retiring the displayed XFB, promoting the queued XFB, and advancing another completed buffer.

facts.value: Implements the HSD video-presentation layer: it owns video configuration and EFB/XFB bookkeeping, installs retrace and GX draw-done callbacks, coordinates framebuffer copies, and exposes synchronization and configuration operations around the Dolphin VI and GX APIs.
facts.rationale: At the current checkout head, HSD_VIInit initializes VI and the global EFB/XFB records, registers VI retrace and GX draw-done callbacks, configures output, and submits the initial EFB-to-XFB copy. The asynchronous-copy and completion routines show that these facilities form one framebuffer-presentation layer rather than unrelated wrappers.

evidence.why: Shows initialization of VI, EFB/XFB state, retrace and draw-done callbacks, output configuration, and the initial EFB-to-XFB copy.
Shows GX copy completion tracking, asynchronous XFB copying, and presentation-state transitions managed by the unit.

facts.value: The unit maintains a presentation state machine around one EFB and up to three XFB slots. Configured XFB slots initialize as FREE and absent slots as NONE, while the EFB initializes as FREE. An asynchronous copy advances a selected XFB through DRAWING and WAITDONE; draw completion changes WAITDONE to NEXT when no frame is already queued, or to DRAWDONE when a NEXT frame exists. At post-retrace, DISPLAY becomes FREE, NEXT becomes DISPLAY, and any DRAWDONE frame advances to NEXT. The draw-done callback state separately tracks whether a GX completion is pending and the integer argument forwarded to its registered callback.
facts.rationale: The current initialization code establishes the initial EFB/XFB and callback states. The asynchronous-copy path requires DRAWING before changing an XFB to WAITDONE and arms GX draw completion with its index. HSD_VIDrawDoneXFB conditionally selects NEXT or DRAWDONE, the post-retrace callback performs the DISPLAY/FREE/NEXT rotation, and the GX callback clears its pending flag and forwards its saved argument.

evidence.why: Shows present XFB slots initialized as FREE, absent slots as NONE, the EFB initialized as FREE, and draw-done waiting state initialized as clear.
Shows the DRAWING-to-WAITDONE transition, GX draw-done arming with the XFB index, and conditional WAITDONE-to-NEXT-or-DRAWDONE completion.
Shows post-retrace transitions from DISPLAY to FREE, NEXT to DISPLAY, and DRAWDONE to NEXT.
Shows the GX draw-done callback clearing the pending flag and forwarding the stored integer argument to its registered callback.
